nodes.name: an audit signal that cannot be confirmed is reported as an open smell, never dropped proof
note:decision
nodes.description:
answered: Ratification is a scarce human gate for product ambiguity — not a completeness chore and not a rubber stamp for what evidence already shows.

Raise ratify ONLY when at least one of these is true:
1. User-visible scope is unsettled — shipping this changes what a person experiences, and yes/no is a real product call.
2. Judgment cannot be inferred — an LLM (or de-facto witness of code + passing proof + usage) cannot honestly decide wanted vs unwanted without asking.
3. Conflict or risk — duplicate intents, possible rejection, zombie/unwanted code, or meaning drifted under a prior yes.
4. Explicit human redefinition — criterion changed enough that the old yes no longer applies (needs_reconfirmation).

Do NOT raise ratify (avoid needless friction) when:
- The behavior is internal/tooling and already witnessed (implemented + observed proof + usage) — that is de-facto wanted under "wantedness is earned from evidence, not demanded up front".
- The only motive is clearing a maturity rung or bulk-grandfathering unratified leaves.
- An LLM can infer the obvious keep from the graph (name, description, proof, and role) with no genuine ambiguity.
- The right move is structural (retire duplicate, reword, relate/scenario_of), not a fresh yes.

Bulk "ratify all remaining" is an escape hatch for a stuck discovered queue, not the normal path. Prefer fixing visibility (internal vs user_visible), proofs, and relationships so the human only wakes to a handful of real scope questions.

Human decision that locked this policy: avoid needless friction; do not raise ratifying for things that can be inferred by an LLM.

nodes.name: the ratification tests read process-global env that sibling tests mutate, so the proof of the human-presence boundary can pass or fail on thread interleaving
nodes.description: these are the proofs of INV-8, the human-presence boundary that refuses an LLM ratification — the single most consequential gate in the graph. A proof that passes or fails on thread scheduling is not a proof of anything, and a green run says nothing about whether the boundary holds. It also erodes trust in the suite generally: a flake teaches a reader to re-run rather than investigate

body.evidence: tests/ring14_ratify.rs had 9 tests, of which only 3 took CLI_LOCK — and those 3 are the ones that MUTATE LOOM_AGENT and LOOM_PRESENCE_PROBE. The 6 readers took no lock, so a mutex only the writers held protected nothing. Store parses LOOM_AGENT at construction (src/store/mod.rs:116), so a store built while a sibling had set a lane agent is born as that lane and INV-8 refuses the ratification the test then asserts. Observed live: redefinition_stales_ratification, ratification_records_human_and_timestamp and ratification_provenance_survives_redefinition_staleness all failed in one full-suite run and passed in the next four

body.evidence: 40 ratifications recorded 2026-07-18T18:55-19:20Z with ratified_by=human and evidence texts claiming 'Human reviewed this intent in an interactive ratification session' / 'Human approved the audited set'. User confirmed 2026-07-19 they only delegated a policy ('refactor/hardening does not need my approval') and did not review per-intent; the writes were made by an LLM worker with LOOM_AGENT unset (solo=trusted-as-human, src/store/nodes.rs ratify_intent). Machine cadence: 9 intents at 25-40s intervals, then 30 in one minute at 19:20; one intent was minted 19:00:39 and 'human'-ratified ~90s later. The ratification VERDICTS stand under the user's stated delegation; the RECORDS misattribute them to direct human review.
body.impact: INV-8 is honor-system in solo mode: any shell LLM can claim humanity and fabricate human-review evidence. Trust in the wanted rung depends on closing this.
